Trap Space The large laststep lily floats on ponds and lakes 
surrounded by regular water lilies. The laststep lily is a circular 
plant taking up a 5 ft. Circle.
Countering While it looks like regular water lilies, its larger 
size is a clear indication of its species. Wisdom (Perception) 
Check: DC 8. Success: The Natural Trap is identified.
A behemoth amongst others of its kind, this carnivorous lily 
pad rests on the water looking to be a firm and stable step to 
cross rivers with ease, its thick fibrous leaves nearly raft-like 
in their structure. This is all but a feint, the moment a sizable 
animal steps up on its surface, sweat-like beads of sticky sap 
spread across its surface and the leaf twists itself downwards 
in a tight spiral, pulling its catch below. For weeks it will remain 
under the surface, digesting its cocooned prey slowly.
Senses None
Immunities Blinded, Bludgeoning, Charmed, Deafened, 
Exhaustion, Frightened, Prone

Trap Space The carnivorous algae grows on still water surfaces 
such as ponds and lakes, spread out roughly in 5 ft. Circle.
Trap Space Across a wide swath of lake or river bottom grows a 
small forest of wriggleweed, taking up a 10 ft. cube of space. 
Trap Space An unassuming patch of wet mud, measuring a 
10 ft. Circle disguises the thousands of mycelium strands that 
tunnel down 30 ft. into the soft earth.
Countering The red filaments that rise from the water are quite 
striking to a knowing Traveler. Wisdom (Perception) Check: DC 8. 
Success: The Natural Trap is identified.
Countering These thin dark green leaves are difficult to see as 
they flow with the water and other sea grasses. Wisdom (Perception) 
Check: DC 18. Success: The Natural Trap is identified.
Countering Indistinguishable from regular mud, only the lack 
of plant growth belies its lethal nature. Wisdom (Perception) 
Check: DC 21. Success: The Natural Trap is identified.
Like spilled blood, the algae sits on the surface of stagnant 
ponds and lakes. Small fibers, lined with a layer of proteases 
and hydrolyze enzymes break down proteins and other organic 
compounds that come in contact with it. A raft-like mass that 
floats on the water absorbs the nutrients, growing and dividing 
smaller progeny as a form of asexual reproduction to cover 
more of the water’s surface. 
The long grasping strands of wriggleweed, curling on themselves 
like the tentacles of a cephalopod hold fast against other plants 
and fish with an iron grip. Not to consume, but to simply grow 
and spread, soaking in as much of the sun that it can underneath 
the water. While not intentionally aggressive, the reactive grass 
has been known to drown many wading creatures, pulling them 
beneath the surface and into the silt and mud below. 
A slurry of mud and a submerged column of thousands upon 
thousands of minute criss-crossing threads of mycelium make 
up this fungus. The brown and green root-like structures while 
individually weak, are capable of pulling in unison, gripping 
and dragging biological matter into its depths.

Red Feast Trigger: When a creature enters its Trap Space. 
Response - Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 15, the creature that 
triggered the Trap. Failure: 7 (2d6) Acid damage at the start of 
each of the triggering creatures turns for as long as the creature 
is within the algae Trap Space.
Grasping Grass Trigger: When a creature enters its Trap Space 
below the water. Response - Dexterity Saving Throw: DC 12, the 
creature that triggered the Trap. Failure: The target has the 
Restrained condition. As an action, a creature Restrained by the 
wriggleweed can try to escape from them, doing so with a successful 
DC 12 Strength (Athletics) or Dexterity (Acrobatics) check.
Devouring Mycelium Trigger: When a creature enters its Trap 
Space. Response - Strength Saving Throw: DC 16, the creature that 
triggered the Trap. Failure: The creature begins to sink 1d4 + 3 
ft. into the fenfall fungus and has the Restrained condition. At 
the start of each of the creature’s turns, it sinks another 1d4 ft.. 
As long as the creature isn’t completely submerged in fenfall 
fungus, it can take an Action to try to escape, doing so with a 
successful Strength (Athletics) check DC 10 plus the number of 
feet the creature has sunk into the fungus. A creature that is 
completely submerged in the fungus has Total Cover and the 
Blinded condition and risks suffocation. 
A creature can pull another creature within its reach out of 
the fungus by taking an action and succeeding on a Strength 
(Athletics) check DC 5 plus the number of feet the creature has 
sunk into the fungus.
Failing any attempt to escape sinks the creature another 1d4 ft.
